review_notes: I read the whole file. I also read the sibling `retargetInputStartedCfg` definition and its simp lemmas. I checked the two uses of the `compCfg_*` lemmas, in this file and in Hoare.lean. The proofs here call `simp only [..., complementCfg]` and `dsimp only [complementCfg]`, and use `show ... from rfl`, instead of projection simp lemmas. I did not run Lean, so I don't know whether adding the lemmas shortens or changes any proof. I found no problem with the existing simp calls, and no sign of a rewrite loop or a competing rule. The file has no `@[simp]` attributes at all. Because of that, I only suggest a small, targeted addition of projection lemmas for the embedding.

findings.excerpt:
def complementCfg (tm : TM n) (c : Cfg n tm.Q) : Cfg n (tm.complementTM.Q) :=
  { state := Sum.inl c.state, input := c.input, work := c.work, output := c.output }
findings.problem: The embedding `complementCfg` is a plain `def`. It has no simp lemmas for its projections `.state`, `.input`, `.work` or `.output`. So `(complementCfg tm c).output` and similar terms only normalise by unfolding the definition. In the file this is done through `show (complementCfg tm c_halt).state = Sum.inl c_halt.state from rfl`, `dsimp only [complementCfg]` (twice) and `simp only [TM.step, complementTM, complementCfg]`. Unfolding `complementCfg` inside a big `simp only` set exposes the whole structure literal, so goals can become messier than needed. The sibling definition `retargetInputStartedCfg` in the same library provides `@[simp]` projection lemmas (`_state`, `_input`, `_output`). The two `rfl` identities `compCfg_initCfg` and `compCfg_qstart` are used only through explicit `rw [...] at hsim`. The simplifier therefore cannot normalise `complementCfg tm (tm.initCfg x)` to `tm.complementTM.initCfg x`.
findings.proposed_change:
Add projection lemmas right after the definition and mark them `@[simp]`:
`@[simp] theorem complementCfg_state (tm : TM n) (c : Cfg n tm.Q) : (complementCfg tm c).state = Sum.inl c.state := rfl`
Add `complementCfg_input`, `complementCfg_work` and `complementCfg_output` in the same way, each by `rfl`.
Then replace `show (complementCfg tm c_halt).state = Sum.inl c_halt.state from rfl` and the `dsimp only [complementCfg]` calls with `complementCfg_state` and the other projection lemmas. This lets `complementTM_step_sim` and `complementTM_rewind_and_flip` avoid unfolding `complementCfg`. Optionally tag `compCfg_initCfg` and `compCfg_qstart` with `@[simp]`. Their left sides are headed by `complementCfg` and are more specific than the right sides, so there is no loop. Skip the tags if the `complementCfg tm (tm.initCfg x)` shape is not wanted as a simp-normal form.
findings.benefit: Terms like `(complementCfg tm c).output.cells` would simplify the same way everywhere, without unfolding the definition. This matches the convention of `retargetInputStartedCfg`. Proofs about `complementCfg`, here and in later users such as Hoare.lean, could use `simp` instead of unfolding and `show ... from rfl`. The projection lemmas cannot loop, because their right-hand sides contain no `complementCfg`.

evidence.excerpt: @[simp] theorem retargetInputStartedCfg_state (M : TM k) (y : List Bool)
show (complementCfg tm c_halt).state = Sum.inl c_halt.state from rfl,
